economics.competition-explain.0012.all: Existing gyms lose customers to the cheaper rival, so revenue/profits fall; they may cut membership prices or improve service/facilities (non-price competition) to retain members in Valencia.

economics.competition-mcq-auth.0004.all: large profits can fund research and development

economics.competition-mcq-class.0006.all: There is heavy use of branding and advertising (note: 'price maker' arguably also applies)

economics.competition-mcq-def.0007.all: When firms agree to work together for example to fix prices, rather than compete

economics.competition-state.0004.all: Lower prices (or more choice, better quality).

economics.competition-state-class.0003.all: Many buyers and sellers (or low barriers to entry, firms are price takers).

economics.conflicts-analyse-1.0001.all: 8% growth raises AD faster than capacity -> demand-pull inflation 7.5%; low unemployment 4.1% raises wage pressure (cost-push); higher incomes raise imports widening deficit; so growth/low unemployment conflict with price stability and BoP; reducing inflation would raise unemployment.

economics.conflicts-analyse-2.0003.all: Expanding manufacturing raises output, jobs, incomes; but increases pollution, emissions, deforestation (negative externalities), depleting resources and harming future growth/health costs; trade-off.

economics.conflicts-assess-1.0008.all: For: inflation 8.3% erodes purchasing power, competitiveness, deficit widening; contractionary monetary/fiscal policy cools AD. Against: higher unemployment from 3.8%, lost output, inflation may be cost-push/temporary; supply-side policies better. Judgement.

economics.conflicts-assess-2.0006.all: Growth: jobs, incomes, tax revenue, export earnings from oil. Environment: pollution, forest loss, climate, health costs, unsustainable; oil finite. Can be balanced via regulation, taxes, sustainable growth. Judgement depends on development level.

economics.conflicts-describe.0003.all: Rapid growth raises AD above productive capacity, causing demand-pull inflation.

economics.conflicts-evaluate-1.0006.all: Plan: 9.1% inflation harms real incomes/competitiveness and BoP; raising interest rates/taxes reduces AD; but raises unemployment from 4.1%, lost output; depends on cause of inflation and size of slowdown; supply-side alternative; judgement.

economics.conflicts-evaluate-2.0001.all: Plan: mining growth -> jobs, exports, tax revenue for public services; vs pollution, forest loss, externalities, finite resources, long-term costs; regulation/taxes allow both; judgement.

economics.conflicts-explain.0017.all: Coal mining and burning release CO2 and pollutants (negative externalities), damage land/water and health; so higher growth and exports come at the cost of environmental damage in Sundara.

economics.costs-analyse-1.0004.all: Fuel +17% and wage rise increase variable costs and total costs; with a small profit, profit may become a loss; may raise prices (lose customers if elastic) or cut costs; reduced investment.

economics.costs-analyse-2.0002.all: Fixed costs rise above Rs 6,000, but doubling output spreads fixed costs, lowering average fixed cost/average cost (economies of scale); variable costs rise with output; risk if demand doesn't rise.

economics.costs-analyse-3.0001.all: Profit = TR - TC; TR up 12% but TC up more (higher raw materials, wages, rent, energy), so gap narrows; possibly lower efficiency/diseconomies.

economics.costs-assess-1.0001.all: For: covers 21% fuel and wage costs, protects profit. Against: passengers may switch to other transport if demand elastic, revenue may fall; alternatives: cut costs, efficiency. Depends on PED/competition.

economics.costs-assess-2.0006.all: For: doubled output, lower average cost, higher revenue. Against: higher fixed costs, need demand, finance/risk. Judgement depends on demand.

economics.costs-assess-3.0001.all: Raise price (depends on PED), cut costs (cheaper suppliers, efficiency), increase sales via advertising; each has drawbacks. Judgement.

economics.costs-data.0018.b: TR up 9% but TC rose faster (raw materials, wages, energy), so profit = TR - TC fell.
economics.costs-data.0018.c: Plan: raise price (PED), cut costs, increase sales/marketing, efficiency; drawbacks of each; judgement.

economics.costs-define2.0003.all: The total cost of production (1): fixed costs plus variable costs (1).

economics.costs-evaluate-1.0005.all: Plan: higher fares cover 34% fuel and wage costs; but customers may switch if elastic; competitors; alternatives cutting costs; judgement depends on PED.

economics.costs-evaluate-2.0002.all: Plan: doubled output and lower AC vs higher fixed costs, demand uncertainty, finance; judgement.

economics.costs-evaluate-3.0004.all: Plan: raise price, cut costs, increase sales; evaluate each; judgement.

economics.costs-explain.0004.all: Rent is a fixed cost; 19% increase raises fixed and total costs, so Hiroshi's profit falls unless he raises prices.

economics.competition-mcq-class.0006.fix: Replace B with a clearly non-oligopoly feature, e.g. 'There are no barriers to entry' or 'Firms are price takers'.
